recipes.title: Active users & event volume over time (DAU/WAU/MAU)
recipes.when_to_use: How many unique users / events over time, at day/week/month grain.
recipes.notes: DAU/MAU ratio (stickiness) = active_users at day vs month grain.
recipes.hack: count_distinct of the entity key = unique actors; group_by {time: metric_time, grain} turns any measure into a time series. Extrapolate: unique-X-over-time = count_distinct(entity) scoped to the X event.

recipes.title: Metric sliced by a user attribute
recipes.when_to_use: Revenue / payers / ARPPU broken down by country, platform, media_source, acquisition_type or campaign_id.
recipes.notes: User attributes via the implicit events.user -> users.user join; campaign_id is a plain string attribute on dim_users (1-hop, like country/platform) — there is no separate campaigns table.
recipes.hack: Any measure + group_by [{ model: 'users', attribute: '<attr>' }] makes the semantic layer auto-join the user dimension — no join written. Extrapolate: segment ANY metric by ANY user attribute the same way.

recipes.title: 2-step conversion funnel (level_started -> level_completed)
recipes.when_to_use: Step conversion / completion rate between two events within a window.
recipes.notes: Conversion base/conversion measures must be count_distinct. No native N-step funnel; chain 2-step conversions or use derived over step counts.
recipes.hack: A funnel step = an event narrowed by an event_data property value, counted as count_distinct(user); step conversion = ratio(next_step / prev_step). Extrapolate: any 2-step drop-off.

recipes.title: Multi-step funnel where each step = event + property value
recipes.when_to_use: Onboarding/activation funnels whose steps are the SAME event with a different property value (e.g. tutorial step_id=step_1 -> step_2 -> step_3), with step-to-step conversion.
recipes.notes: A funnel step is a measure scoped by event_name + a property `where` (event_data value). Steps chain as 2-step conversion metrics (s1->s2, s2->s3); multiply/compose for end-to-end. Could also key the step on level_id, screen_to, placement, etc.
recipes.hack: Chain one count_distinct(user) measure per step (event + property value) and ratio metrics between consecutive steps. Extrapolate: any ordered N-step sequence.

recipes.title: N-day retention (D1/D7) via conversion window
recipes.when_to_use: Share of newly-acquired users who return (start a session) within N days of first launch.
recipes.notes: Cohort = users with a first_launch (acquisition); returned = users who start a new_session within the window. base_measure and conversion_measure are DIFFERENT events so the rate is meaningful (not identically 1.0). Approximates N-day retention via conversion window; exact point-in-time D-N retention is not native to MetricFlow.
recipes.hack: Retention = a conversion metric (base = first/install event, conversion = a later activity event) with window = 'N day'. Extrapolate: change N or the base/return events for any Dn.

recipes.title: Acquisition-cohort grid (install date x activity)
recipes.when_to_use: Cohort table: metric by install_date cohort and activity day.
recipes.notes: Group by install_date (cohort) and metric_time (age). Cumulative LTV per cohort can layer a cumulative metric.
recipes.hack: Pivot a retention measure by install-cohort (a time dimension) against age-in-days. Extrapolate: any cohort-attribute × age-bucket grid.

recipes.title: Behavioral cohort: users who did / didn't do event X
recipes.when_to_use: Segment users by whether they performed a behavior (e.g. purchased), then compare metrics.
recipes.notes: Split did/didn't with a Metric() in --where, e.g. `{{ Metric('behavior_purchases', group_by=['user']) }} > 0`.
recipes.hack: Split the population by a behavioral flag (did event X) then measure later behavior on each arm. Extrapolate: any 'did A → compare B' cohort.

recipes.title: Visit-to-purchase conversion (native conversion metric)
recipes.when_to_use: Share of visitors who purchase within a window.
recipes.notes: Use constant_properties to require the same product across base/conversion events when relevant.
recipes.hack: conversion metric linking two events by the shared user entity (base=visit, conversion=purchase). Extrapolate: any A→B funnel within a window.

recipes.title: Level progression: completion, attempts, time per level
recipes.when_to_use: Per-level difficulty: starts, completes, completion rate, avg time/attempts.
recipes.notes: Group by the JSON-extracted level_id dimension. Churn-at-level derived from starts of level N vs N+1 in post-processing.
recipes.hack: Group an event measure by a numeric event_data ordinal (level_id) and ratio adjacent values = progression/drop-off. Extrapolate: any per-step numeric progression.

recipes.title: Monetization: revenue, ARPPU, AOV, by product/channel/day
recipes.when_to_use: IAP revenue, payers, ARPPU, average order value over time and by segment/product.
recipes.notes: LTV curve = cumulative revenue over metric_time by acquisition cohort (needs time spine).
recipes.hack: Per-X average = a value measure ÷ a population measure via a ratio metric (revenue ÷ users = ARPU; ÷ payers = ARPPU). Extrapolate: any 'total per entity' = ratio(sum, count_distinct).

recipes.title: Ad monetization: ad revenue & impressions by network/placement
recipes.when_to_use: Ad revenue, impressions, eCPM-style splits by ad_network/placement/ad_type.
recipes.notes: Ad revenue lives on ad_finished.revenue. eCPM = rev_per_imp * 1000 (post-process).
recipes.hack: Aggregate a value property (revenue) grouped by its categorical context properties (network/format/placement). Extrapolate: sum(value) by its descriptor dimensions for any breakdown.

recipes.title: In-game economy: coin sources vs sinks
recipes.when_to_use: Coins earned (income) vs spent (outcome) by source/placement.
recipes.notes: net_coins is a derived metric (income - outcome). Source/sink breakdown via source_type.
recipes.hack: Two oppositely-scoped sum measures + a derived expr (in − out) = net flow / balance. Extrapolate: any signed two-sided quantity (faucets vs sinks, credits vs debits).

recipes.title: Stickiness (DAU/MAU) & active base over time
recipes.when_to_use: How sticky the product is and how the active base evolves.
recipes.notes: DAU/MAU ratio = active_users at day grain / active_users at month grain.
recipes.hack: Query the SAME count_distinct measure at two grains (day vs month) and divide = stickiness. Extrapolate: ratio of one measure across two windows.

recipes.title: A/B test — conversion rate by variant (with significance)
recipes.when_to_use: Compare a conversion rate (e.g. purchase) between experiment variants and test whether the difference is significant.
recipes.notes: The native-model pipeline builds a model whose rows are n + conversions per variant (exposed = users with in-window events). Then call ab_test with metric=proportion: control = the control variant_group row, variants = the rest. For a continuous metric (revenue/ARPU per user), aggregate per-user then per-variant mean+stddev and call ab_test with metric=mean.
recipes.hack: Join the experiments source, window events from assigned_at onward (firstExposure — no end bound), flag conversion per user (compute case → aggregate max), then aggregate n + conversions per variant and call ab_test. Extrapolate: per-variant rate (proportion) or per-user mean+stddev (Welch) for ANY experiment metric.

recipes.title: Cumulative & period-to-date revenue (running totals)
recipes.when_to_use: Running total of revenue over time, and month-to-date (resets each month). Showcases the cumulative metric type.
recipes.notes: cumulative with no window = running total from the start; grain_to_date:month = month-to-date (resets monthly). Add `window` (e.g. "7 day") for a trailing rolling-window cumulative.
recipes.hack: cumulative metric over a sum measure = running total; grain_to_date resets each period (MTD/WTD); add a window for a trailing rolling total. Extrapolate: any accumulating quantity over time.

recipes.title: Blended revenue: IAP + ad revenue capped at 1 USD/impression
recipes.when_to_use: Combine two revenue streams into one blended total: IAP price in USD + ad revenue capped to [0,1] USD/impression. Both legs are ALREADY USD — never divide by 100.

stages.name: iap_usd
stages.sql: case when event_name = 'iap_purchase_completed' then cast(price_in_usd_of_event_data as float64) end

stages.name: ad_usd
stages.sql: case when event_name = 'ad_finished' then least(greatest(cast(revenue_of_event_data as float64), 0.0), 1.0) end

stages.name: blended_usd
stages.sql: coalesce(case when event_name = 'iap_purchase_completed' then cast(price_in_usd_of_event_data as float64) end, 0.0) + coalesce(case when event_name = 'ad_finished' then least(greatest(cast(revenue_of_event_data as float64), 0.0), 1.0) end, 0.0)

recipes.notes: ad_revenue is defined here as: ad_finished only, cast to float64, clamped to [0,1] USD per impression. The clamp WINSORIZES (an outlier becomes 1.0, the row is not dropped), so a governed sum measure cannot reproduce it — that is why this recipe is a native pipeline and not a semantic model. revenue_of_event_data is ALREADY USD: dividing it by 100 is wrong, and the same money is repeated on ad_loaded/ad_started/ad_revenue/ad_finished, so exactly ONE of those events may be summed. The IAP leg is the IN-GAME price: iap_purchase_completed before tax, unvalidated. A BI inapp figure built from validated store/attribution purchases is a DIFFERENT quantity and will not match — if the question is about billed revenue, take it from there, not from here.
recipes.hack: A per-row clamp lives in compute op=raw and nowhere else: least/greatest around the value, then sum it — a governed sum measure aggregates a column, it cannot bound each row first. Extrapolate: any quantity that must be bounded, floored or conditionally zeroed BEFORE aggregation — write that row expression in compute op=raw and aggregate it at the reporting grain.

recipes.title: A/B test — revenue per user by variant (Welch t-test)
recipes.when_to_use: Compare a CONTINUOUS metric (revenue/ARPU/time per user) between experiment variants and test significance.
recipes.hack: Per-user continuous A/B: window events to the assignment period, coalesce the per-event value to 0, sum per user (one value per exposed user), then per variant compute n + avg + stddev and call ab_test metric=mean (Welch). Extrapolate: ANY per-user continuous metric (revenue, session time, items) between variants.
recipes.notes: mean A/B needs per-variant n, mean and stddev of a PER-USER value (aggregate per user first, then per variant). ab_test metric=mean runs Welch t-test: control = control variant_group row, variants = the rest.

recipes.title: A/B test — CUPED variance reduction (pre-experiment covariate)
recipes.when_to_use: Compare a continuous metric between variants with MORE POWER by adjusting for each user's pre-experiment value of the same metric (CUPED).
recipes.hack: CUPED = variance reduction via a pre-experiment covariate: per user compute Y (metric from assigned_at onward) and X (same metric BEFORE assigned_at) with two compute-case windows, then per variant emit the sufficient sums n, ΣY, ΣY², ΣX, ΣX², ΣXY (sum of Y, Y*Y, X, X*X, X*Y) and call ab_test metric=cuped. Extrapolate: any continuous A/B gains power when a correlated pre-period covariate exists — no per-user data leaves SQL, only the 6 sums.
recipes.notes: CUPED needs a PRE-experiment covariate (the same metric before assignment); it removes its variance, raising power, and reduces to a plain t-test when there is no pre-period signal. Pass per-variant sufficient sums; the tool computes the pooled theta and runs Welch on the adjusted means.

recipes.title: A/B test — ratio metric via the delta method (e.g. level completion rate)
recipes.when_to_use: Compare a RATIO metric between variants where the unit of analysis is finer than the randomization unit — e.g. levels completed per level started, or clicks per impression, when users (not attempts) are randomized.
recipes.notes: The native-model pipeline builds a model whose rows carry, per variant: n (users) plus the per-user numerator/denominator sums and their squares/cross-product. Then call ab_test with metric=ratio: control = the control variant_group row, variants = the rest. The ratio is Σnumerator/Σdenominator; the delta method turns the per-user sums into a cluster-robust variance, so attempts within a user are not treated as independent.
recipes.hack: For a ratio metric whose denominator is counted at a finer grain than the randomization unit (events/sessions per user), aggregate numerator & denominator PER USER first so each user is one independent observation, then carry forward their squares (num², den²) and cross-product (num·den) and sum per variant. ab_test metric=ratio applies the delta method for the correct (cluster-robust) variance — a plain proportion test on pooled events would understate it. Extrapolate: CTR (clicks/impressions), completion rate, ARPDAU, etc.

recipes.title: A/B guardrail — Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) check
recipes.when_to_use: BEFORE trusting any lift: verify the observed per-variant split matches the intended one. A mismatch means randomization or logging is broken and the whole experiment is invalid.
recipes.notes: The native-model pipeline builds a model whose rows are the number of EXPOSED users per variant (distinct users with in-window events). Feed those counts to srm_check: it runs a χ² goodness-of-fit against the intended split (equal by default; pass expected_ratio for an uneven design). p < 0.001 ⇒ srm_detected=true ⇒ STOP and fix assignment/logging before reading any metric. This is a guardrail, not a metric — run it alongside the metric recipes (conversion/revenue/ratio/cuped).
recipes.hack: Count distinct exposed users per variant in the warehouse, then compare observed vs intended counts with srm_check (χ² goodness-of-fit). Extrapolate: ANY 'observed category counts vs an expected split' sanity check (traffic allocation, platform mix, day-of-week balance) is the same χ² test.

recipes.title: A/B planning — sample size & minimum detectable effect (power)
recipes.when_to_use: BEFORE launching, to size the test (how many users per variant to detect a target effect), or given the traffic you have, to find the smallest effect you can detect (MDE). Also AFTER an inconclusive test, to tell 'no effect' apart from 'underpowered'.
recipes.notes: sample_size is a pure calculation (no warehouse). Provide a baseline rate (metric=proportion) or a stddev (metric=mean) plus EXACTLY ONE of mde (→ required n per group) or n (→ minimum detectable effect). Estimate the baseline/stddev from a monetization_metrics or active_users_trend query first, then plan. Pair every ab_test with an up-front MDE so a non-significant result can be read correctly.
recipes.hack: Up-front power analysis: baseline/stddev + target effect → required n per group; or n → MDE. Run it before the test to size it and after an inconclusive test to check it was powered. Extrapolate: any two-arm comparison (proportion z-test or mean t-test).

recipes.title: Game engagement: sessions, unit starts/completions, session length
recipes.when_to_use: Sessions, level/puzzle starts & completions, completion rate and avg session length, by progression chain/mechanic.
recipes.notes: Governed measures (count* / sum of a numeric event_data property scoped by event_name): session counts and duration, units started/completed. NOTE: playtime here is the RAW complete_time; a version bounded to [0,3600]s per row needs a native pipeline, because a governed measure cannot clamp before summing (see game_playtime_native).
recipes.hack: Count an event = count(*) scoped by event_name; rate = ratio(next/prev); per-event avg = ratio(sum(value)/count(event)). Extrapolate: any event-count metric, any adjacent-stage rate, and any per-event average built the same way.

recipes.title: Coin economy: coins earned vs spent (coin value) by source
recipes.when_to_use: Coins earned (income) vs spent (outcome) in coin value, net flow, by source/operation type.
recipes.notes: Governed sum of value_in_coins (coin value) scoped to currency_income/outcome; net_coins is a derived metric. Negatives are summed AS THEY ARE here: a version that floors each row at zero (greatest(x,0)) needs a native pipeline, since a governed measure cannot floor before summing. For raw resource amount swap value_in_coins_of_event_data -> amount_of_event_data.
recipes.hack: Two oppositely-scoped sum measures + derived (in - out) = net flow. Extrapolate: any signed two-sided quantity (faucets vs sinks, credits vs debits) modelled as two scoped sums plus a derived difference.

recipes.title: Ad delivery funnel: starts, fills, impressions, revenue
recipes.when_to_use: Ad starts->fills->impressions funnel, fill/show rates, revenue & eCPM, by network/placement/format.
recipes.notes: Governed: ad_fills = count of ad_loaded with status=success (per-measure where); funnel rates as ratio metrics; eCPM = rev_per_imp*1000. Revenue here is summed UNCAPPED; a capped ad revenue ([0,1] USD/imp) and clamped display/latency need the native pipeline, because a governed measure cannot bound a row before summing (ad_quality_native).
recipes.hack: Delivery funnel = count(*) per stage event (+ where on status) chained as ratio metrics. Extrapolate: any staged delivery funnel — chain count(*) per stage event into ratio metrics between adjacent stages.

recipes.title: Game playtime (complete_time clamped to [0,3600])
recipes.when_to_use: Playtime per completed unit: complete_time clamped to [0,3600]s per row, summed by day. Needs a native pipeline because a governed measure cannot clamp before summing.

stages.name: playtime_val
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_completed','puzzle_completed') then greatest(least(cast(complete_time_of_event_data as float64), 3600), 0) end

recipes.notes: Playtime per completed unit with complete_time clamped to [0,3600] seconds per row, then summed. Read the result via get_query_result; group_by event_date.
recipes.hack: Clamp = greatest(least(x, hi), lo) inside a compute op=raw, then aggregate sum. Extrapolate: any per-row value that needs bounding before aggregation — clamp inside compute op=raw, then sum.

recipes.title: Ad quality: capped revenue, clamped display & waterfall latency
recipes.when_to_use: Ad quality with per-row bounds: revenue capped [0,1] USD/imp, display_duration clamped [0,150]s, waterfall latency ms/1000 clamped [0,300]s + eligible-event count (for avg latency).

stages.name: ad_revenue_val
stages.sql: case when event_name = 'ad_finished' then least(greatest(cast(revenue_of_event_data as float64), 0.0), 1.0) end

stages.name: display_val
stages.sql: case when event_name = 'ad_finished' then greatest(0.0, least(safe_cast(display_duration_of_event_data as float64), 150.0)) end

stages.name: latency_val
stages.sql: case when ((event_name = 'ad_loaded' and lower(ad_type_of_event_data) in ('rewarded','interstitial')) or (lower(ad_type_of_event_data) = 'banner' and event_name = 'ad_finished')) and coalesce(status_of_event_data, 'success') = 'success' then greatest(least(safe_cast(waterfall_latency_of_additional_info_of_event_data as float64) / 1000, 300.0), 0.0) end

stages.name: latency_evt
stages.sql: case when ((event_name = 'ad_loaded' and lower(ad_type_of_event_data) in ('rewarded','interstitial')) or (lower(ad_type_of_event_data) = 'banner' and event_name = 'ad_finished')) and coalesce(status_of_event_data, 'success') = 'success' then 1.0 else 0.0 end

recipes.notes: Three per-row bounded quantities, each summed: ad revenue capped to [0,1] USD per impression, display duration clamped to [0,150]s, waterfall latency in ms/1000 clamped to [0,300]s — plus the count of latency-eligible events. Avg latency = latency_sum / latency_events_count; avg display = display_sum / impressions (post-process or a downstream compute).
recipes.hack: Clamps/conditions as compute op=raw per row, summed; ratios computed on the result. Extrapolate: any per-row conditional quantity summed into a total, with ratios derived on the aggregated result rather than per row.

recipes.title: Game state snapshots at unit start/completion (balances, hints used)
recipes.when_to_use: Coins/lives/skill balances at level/puzzle start and completion, total hints used, and total hint/booster balance count — summed by day (divide by units_*_count for averages).

stages.name: st_coins
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_started','puzzle_started') then cast(coins_balance_of_state as float64) end

stages.name: cp_coins
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_completed','puzzle_completed') then cast(coins_balance_of_state as float64) end

stages.name: st_lives
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_started','puzzle_started') then cast(lives_balance_of_state as float64) end

stages.name: cp_lives
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_completed','puzzle_completed') then cast(lives_balance_of_state as float64) end

stages.name: st_skill
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_started','puzzle_started') then cast(skill_points_of_state as float64) end

stages.name: cp_skill
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_completed','puzzle_completed') then cast(skill_points_of_state as float64) end

stages.name: cp_res_used
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_completed','puzzle_completed') then (coalesce(cast(hint_open_first_letter_used_of_event_data as int64),0)+coalesce(cast(hint_open_any_letter_used_of_event_data as int64),0)+coalesce(cast(hint_open_several_letters_used_of_event_data as int64),0)+coalesce(cast(hints_cancel_used_of_event_data as int64),0)+coalesce(cast(hints_shuffle_used_of_event_data as int64),0)+coalesce(cast(hints_clear_used_of_event_data as int64),0)+coalesce(cast(hints_magnet_used_of_event_data as int64),0)+coalesce(cast(hint_open_cell_used_of_event_data as int64),0)) end

recipes.notes: Balances captured ON the unit_started / unit_completed events (coins, lives, skill), total hints used, and total hint/booster balance count — each summed by day. State columns are not aggregatable as governed measures, so this uses a native pipeline.
recipes.hack: Snapshot = state column captured on the event, summed; per-unit average = snapshot_sum / units_*_count. Extrapolate: any state column carried on an event — sum it and divide by the count of the unit it was captured on.

recipes.title: Hint/booster balance coin-value at unit start/completion (per-app weighting)
recipes.when_to_use: Coin-value of the player's hint/booster balance at level/puzzle start and completion, each hint weighted by a per-app coin price.

stages.name: st_coins_value
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_started','puzzle_started') then (coalesce(cast(hint_open_first_letter_balance_of_state as int64),0)*(case app_id_of_main_data when 'fillwords' then 100 when 'sky_words' then 100 when 'tile_trip' then 10 when 'word_pizza' then 50 when 'word_search_sea' then 35 when 'word_spells' then 100 else 0 end)+coalesce(cast(hint_open_any_letter_balance_of_state as int64),0)*(case app_id_of_main_data when 'sky_words' then 200 when 'tile_trip' then 20 when 'word_pizza' then 100 when 'word_search_sea' then 70 when 'word_spells' then 200 else 0 end)+coalesce(cast(hint_open_several_letters_balance_of_state as int64),0)*(case app_id_of_main_data when 'sky_words' then 300 when 'tile_trip' then 60 when 'word_pizza' then 150 when 'word_search_sea' then 100 when 'word_spells' then 300 else 0 end)+coalesce(cast(hint_magnet_balance_of_state as int64),0)*(case app_id_of_main_data when 'tile_trip' then 40 else 0 end)) end

stages.name: cp_coins_value
stages.sql: case when event_name in ('level_completed','puzzle_completed') then (coalesce(cast(hint_open_first_letter_balance_of_state as int64),0)*(case app_id_of_main_data when 'fillwords' then 100 when 'sky_words' then 100 when 'tile_trip' then 10 when 'word_pizza' then 50 when 'word_search_sea' then 35 when 'word_spells' then 100 else 0 end)+coalesce(cast(hint_open_any_letter_balance_of_state as int64),0)*(case app_id_of_main_data when 'sky_words' then 200 when 'tile_trip' then 20 when 'word_pizza' then 100 when 'word_search_sea' then 70 when 'word_spells' then 200 else 0 end)+coalesce(cast(hint_open_several_letters_balance_of_state as int64),0)*(case app_id_of_main_data when 'sky_words' then 300 when 'tile_trip' then 60 when 'word_pizza' then 150 when 'word_search_sea' then 100 when 'word_spells' then 300 else 0 end)+coalesce(cast(hint_magnet_balance_of_state as int64),0)*(case app_id_of_main_data when 'tile_trip' then 40 else 0 end)) end

recipes.notes: Coin-value of the player's hint/booster balance at unit start and completion: each hint type weighted by that app's coin price (a hint type with no price for an app contributes 0), summed by day.
recipes.hack: Per-app weighting = nested CASE on app_id inside a compute op=raw; summed by day. Extrapolate: any per-app or per-segment weighting — a nested CASE inside compute op=raw, aggregated by the reporting grain.
